# Video: Federal Leaders Tour Cavco Plant to Explore Housing Solutions


Published On: November 3, 2026


•


1 min read


•


(L to R): Ariz. Rep. Eli Crane, HUD Secretary Scott Turner, Dr. Lesli Gooch, CEO Manufactured Housing Institute, Bill Boor, Cavco President & CEO and Todd Jensen, General Manager, Cavco - Phoenix.


---


PHOENIX – HUD Secretary Scott Turner got a firsthand look at manufactured home production on Oct. 26, touring Cavco’s Phoenix plant just days after President Trump signed an executive order creating a Task Force on Manufactured Housing Innovation.


Arizona Rep. Eli Crane joined the visit, along with Dr. Lesli Gooch of the Manufactured Housing Institute and Thomas Dunn of MHI Arizona. Cavco President and CEO Bill Boor and Phoenix General Manager Todd Jensen guided the group through the facility and spoke about how factory-built homes can ease the housing shortage. According to Crane’s office, officials also discussed modernizing outdated codes and cutting regulations that raise building costs.


The Oct. 22 order gives the task force, co-chaired by HUD and the Federal Housing Finance Agency, 180 days to deliver recommendations. It is aimed at trimming duplicate federal inspections and certifications, clearing obstacles to modern manufacturing and using federal financing to spur production.


Turner praised Cavco’s faster build times, reduced waste and innovation, and said the country needs 5 million to 7 million more housing units. He called the 50-year-old HUD code outdated and pointed to the recent ROAD to Housing Act as a step toward modernizing it. Crane said seeing plant operations in person made the issues far clearer than discussions on Capitol Hill.


Boor said the law’s removal of the chassis requirement will let Cavco design for more uses and reach more areas, including urban markets.
